description: Quantum correction parameters for hydrogen isotopologues. de Boer quantum parameter and Feynman-Hibbs effective potential corrections.

de_boer_lambda_star.description: Reduced de Boer quantum parameter Λ* = h/(σ*sqrt(m*ε)). Higher values indicate stronger quantum effects.
de_boer_lambda_star.source: Souers UCRL-52628 Ch.2; de Boer 1948; Hirschfelder et al. Molecular Theory of Gases (1954)
de_boer_lambda_star.notes: Classical limit: Λ* → 0. Noble gases: He=2.67, Ne=0.59, Ar=0.19. All H-isotopes are strongly quantum.

feynman_hibbs_correction.description: Second-order Feynman-Hibbs effective potential correction to fugacity coefficient. Form: ln(φ_correction) = α/T^2, where α depends on mass and LJ parameters.
feynman_hibbs_correction.source: Feynman & Hibbs 1965; Sesé 1993; Kim et al. 1986 (Quantum corrections to second virial coeff)
feynman_hibbs_correction.notes: Negative alpha means quantum effects INCREASE fugacity (reduce intermolecular attraction). Valid above ~14 K. Magnitude decreases with molecular mass as expected (heavier = more classical).

critical_properties_quantum_corrected.description: Quantum effects shift Tc and Pc relative to classical corresponding states. These are the actual measured values (already include quantum effects).
critical_properties_quantum_corrected.notes: Negative acentric factors are characteristic of quantum fluids (He, H2, Ne). Classical SRK/PR EOS with ω<0 gives poor α(T); quantum correction needed.
